useCase.name: Record a longer-lived item on the asset register when it is bought, with the voucher that paid for it

intent.name: asset.register
intent.summary: Put a longer-lived item on the asset register when it is bought, with the voucher that paid for it.
routesHere: register the new Epson projector against voucher PV-2026-000633

routesHere.text: naya projector asset register mein daal dein
routesHere.gloss: put the new projector on the asset register

routesHere.text: ye laptop register kar dein, voucher lagi hui hai
routesHere.gloss: register this laptop, the voucher is attached

routesHere.text: lab ka naya microscope register par le aayein
routesHere.gloss: bring the lab's new microscope onto the register

routesHere: add the new photocopier to the register

request.text: ye asset register se mita dein
request.gloss: delete this asset from the register

routesElsewhere.note: An asset is never deleted. One that leaves the school is disposed of through its own route and stays readable, since the voucher, the maintenance history and the verifications all reference it (BR-8, E7).

request.text: ye kis ke naam kar dein?
request.gloss: assign it to somebody

routesElsewhere.note: Registering an asset assigns it to nobody. Assigning it to a room, a person or a department is a separate act with its own trigger (BR-9, E8).

request.text: marker ko bhi register kar dein
request.gloss: register the markers too

routesElsewhere.note: A longer-lived item is registered individually; a consumable is counted as stock. What actually separates the two — a value threshold, an expected life, or the school's judgement — is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (BR-1, OQ-1).

request.text: qeemat khud likh dein, voucher chhod dein
request.gloss: type the value in and skip the voucher

routesElsewhere.note: The value on the register is the value on the voucher and is not typed independently (BR-3, E5), and without a voucher the register and the books can state different values for the same purchase (BR-2, E4).

request.text: ye cheez donate hui thi, koi voucher nahi hai
request.gloss: this was donated, there is no voucher

routesElsewhere.note: The rule requires a voucher and nothing says what a donated or transferred asset holds instead. It is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (BR-2, OQ-5).

steps.note: One step, and the value is not among the inputs: it is taken from the voucher rather than typed (BR-3, E5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A duplicate identifier, a purchase date in the future, a value of zero on the voucher, no voucher at all, or no campus where the school has several — each refuses the registration outright.
plan.atomicity: One write. The asset is on the register and **assigned to nobody** — assigning it is a separate act (BR-9, E8). It is now available to be assigned, maintained, verified and eventually disposed of.

operations.name: asset.register
operations.idempotencyKey: identifier, since an asset is registered once and the identifier is what tells two identical machines apart
operations.purpose: Register an asset with its voucher, warranty and insurance dates.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.notes: The asset tag or serial number, unique across the register (BR-6, E1, BR-10). Two entries for one machine is two assets the school thinks it owns.

parameters.name: asset_name
parameters.notes: 2 to 100 characters.

parameters.name: category_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the categories that match.

parameters.notes: What kind of asset it is. Who maintains the category list is not specified anywhere (OQ-3).

parameters.name: purchase_date
parameters.notes: Not in the future (E2).

parameters.name: expected_life
parameters.notes: In years or months, greater than zero. Recorded and **nothing uses it** — whether depreciation is calculated anywhere is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-2).

parameters.name: voucher_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No payment voucher matches. Where the asset was donated or transferred rather than bought, nothing says what the register holds instead (OQ-5).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the vouchers that match with their dates, payees and amounts.

parameters.notes: The payment voucher that paid for the asset. Required (BR-2, E4) — **the value comes from it** and is never typed independently (BR-3, E5).

parameters.name: warranty_expiry
parameters.notes: When the warranty runs out. One of the two things a school actually needs reminding about, and this register is its natural home (BR-4).

parameters.name: insurance_renewal
parameters.notes: The other (BR-4).

parameters.name: campus_id
parameters.notes: Required where the school has more than one campus (BR-5, E6), so a group knows where its equipment is.

parameters.name: location
parameters.notes: Where the asset is — a room, a laboratory, an office. Not the same as an assignment: this says where it sits, and assigning says who answers for it (BR-1, BR-9).

parameters.name: condition
parameters.notes: Its condition when registered. Changed later through maintenance, not here (UC-18-09).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The asset and what the register now holds about it.

fields.name: asset_id
fields.description: The asset.

fields.name: identifier
fields.description: Its tag, unique across the register (BR-6).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Registered. Assigned to nobody (BR-9, E8).

fields.name: value
fields.description: **Taken from the voucher**, not from the request. Where a different figure was offered, the voucher's is used and the difference is reported (BR-3, E5).

fields.name: voucher
fields.description: What paid for it, so the register and the books can be checked against one another (BR-2).

fields.name: warranty_expiry
fields.description: When the warranty runs out. The school is reminded before it passes — how far before is not specified anywhere (BR-4, OQ-4).

fields.name: insurance_renewal
fields.description: When the insurance must be renewed (BR-4, OQ-4).

fields.name: expected_life
fields.description: Held. Nothing calculates depreciation from it (OQ-2).

fields.name: campus
fields.description: Where it sits, for a group with several (BR-5).

fields.name: next_step
fields.description: Assigning it to a room, a person or a department. Until then nobody answers for it (BR-9).

errors.meaning: The identifier already exists on the register.
errors.note: An asset is registered once; a second registration of the same identifier is refused rather than creating a duplicate (BR-6, BR-10).

errors.meaning: The purchase date is in the future.
The value is zero or less.

errors.note: Without it the register and the books can state different values for the same purchase and neither can be checked against the other (BR-2).

errors.meaning: A value was offered that differs from the voucher.
errors.written: The asset is registered at the voucher's value.
errors.notWritten: The offered figure is not used.
errors.note: The value on the register is the value on the voucher (BR-3).

errors.meaning: The school has several campuses and none was selected.
errors.note: A group with several campuses has to know where its equipment is (BR-5).

planningRules.rule: Never type the value. It comes from the voucher, and a register that says something different from the books about the same purchase leaves neither able to check the other (BR-2, BR-3, E5).

Never register without the voucher, and never invent one. Where the asset was donated or transferred rather than bought, the rule still requires a voucher and nothing says what to hold instead — say so rather than improvising (BR-2, E4, OQ-5).

Ask for the warranty and insurance dates even though neither is required. They are the two things a school actually needs reminding about and this register is their only home — an asset registered without them will never remind anybody of anything (BR-4).
Say that registering assigns it to nobody. The asset is on the register and no person, room or department answers for it until it is assigned (BR-9, E8).

Never decide whether something is an asset or stock. A projector is clearly one and a marker clearly is not, and where the line falls — value, expected life, or the school's judgement — is not defined anywhere (BR-1, OQ-1).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An asset registered in error is not deleted — there is no such control. It leaves the register through disposal, which carries its own approval and its own record, and it stays readable because the voucher, the maintenance history and the verifications all reference it (BR-8, E7).

request.text: naya Epson projector register kar dein, voucher PV-2026-000633 hai, physics lab mein laga hai
request.gloss: register the new Epson projector, voucher PV-2026-000633, it is in the physics lab

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, single campus.

steps.note: The value comes from the voucher (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Ask for the warranty expiry and the insurance renewal before saving — neither is required and this register is the only place they live, so an asset saved without them will never remind anybody. After: report the value taken from the voucher, and that the projector is on the register but assigned to nobody yet.

request.text: ye laptop register kar dein, 95 hazaar ka tha
request.gloss: register this laptop, it cost 95 thousand

steps.note: The voucher's figure is used, not the one in the request (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Registered at PKR 92,400 — the voucher's figure, not the 95,000 in the request. That is deliberate: if the register and the books disagree about what one machine cost, neither can be used to check the other. If 92,400 is wrong, the voucher is where it is corrected.

request.text: ye microscope donate hua tha, register kar dein
request.gloss: this microscope was donated, register it

steps.note: Refused at resolution. A voucher is required and none exists (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: It cannot be registered as written. The rule requires the voucher that paid for the asset, and a donated one has none — the specification does not say what the register should hold instead, and this is a question it raises and leaves open. The school has to decide before donated equipment can go on the register at all.

insurance renewal ki tareekh daal dein

routesElsewhere.note: The value on the register is the value on the voucher and is not typed independently. A wrong value is a wrong voucher (BR-3, E5).

request.gloss: change who it is assigned to

routesElsewhere.note: Where an asset sits and who answers for it are different things, and moving the second is an assignment with its own date, its own authoriser and its own reason (BR-9).

request.gloss: its condition has got worse, change the condition

routesElsewhere.note: Condition changes through maintenance, with what it cost and what was done, rather than by editing the register.

steps.note: One step, and neither the value nor the identifier is among the parameters — the first comes from the voucher and the second is what tells this machine from another (BR-3, BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Nothing is half-changed, and every change is recorded with who made it (BR-7).
plan.atomicity: One write and one row in the asset's history. The history is the record of a register that has been corrected rather than one that was always right (BR-7).

operations.name: asset.update
operations.idempotencyKey: asset_id + the fields submitted, so a double press does not leave two identical rows in the asset's history
operations.purpose: Change what the register holds about an asset.

parameters.name: asset_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No asset on the register matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the assets that match with their identifiers, locations and current holders — two projectors of the same model are told apart only by their tags.

parameters.notes: The asset, named by its tag, its serial number or what it is and where it sits.

parameters.name: asset_name
parameters.notes: The corrected name.

parameters.name: category_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the categories that match.

parameters.notes: Where the asset was filed under the wrong category.

parameters.name: expected_life
parameters.notes: The corrected life. Nothing calculates anything from it (OQ-2).

parameters.name: warranty_expiry
parameters.notes: The warranty date, often added after registration because nobody had the paperwork on the day (BR-4).

parameters.name: insurance_renewal
parameters.notes: The insurance date (BR-4).

parameters.name: campus_id
parameters.notes: Correcting which campus the asset sits at. **Moving it to another campus is a transfer, not a correction** — that is a different act with its own record (UC-18-08 BR-4).

parameters.name: location
parameters.notes: Where the asset is. A room, a laboratory, an office.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What changed and what did not.

fields.name: asset_id
fields.description: The asset.

fields.name: changed
fields.description: Field by field, from and to, with who changed it (BR-7).

fields.name: value
fields.description: Unchanged. It comes from the voucher and is not a parameter here (BR-3).

fields.name: identifier
fields.description: Unchanged. It is what tells two identical machines apart (BR-6).

fields.name: warranty_expiry
fields.description: As it now stands. Where this was empty and is now set, the asset can remind somebody for the first time (BR-4).

fields.name: reminders_now_possible
fields.description: Which reminders this change makes possible — a warranty or insurance date that was blank produced none (BR-4).

errors.meaning: A change would make the identifier match another asset.
errors.note: The identifier is unique across the register (BR-6).

planningRules.rule: Never change the value here. It is the voucher's figure, and a register edited to disagree with the books defeats the reason the voucher is held at all (BR-2, BR-3).

Say when a blank date is being filled for the first time. A warranty or insurance date that was empty produced no reminder at all, so adding it is not a correction but the first time the asset can warn anybody (BR-4).
Never treat a change of campus as a correction. Moving an asset to another campus is a transfer with its own record, because the two mean different things to a group (BR-5, UC-18-08 BR-4).
Say that a change of location is not a change of custodian. Where the asset sits and who answers for it are separate, and only one of them is on this screen (BR-9).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: There is no undo. A further correction is another change and both rows stay in the asset's history (BR-7), which is what makes a register that has been corrected distinguishable from one that was always right.

request.text: projector ki insurance renewal ki tareekh daal dein, 1 July 2027

resolvedPlans.outcome: Recorded. Worth saying: this asset produced no insurance reminder before, because the date was blank — the register only reminds about dates somebody has put in it. Its warranty date is still empty.

operations.name: assets.read
operations.purpose: List assets with their values, locations, conditions and expiry dates.

parameters.name: category_phrase

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the categories that match.

parameters.notes: Where the question is about one kind of asset.

parameters.name: location
parameters.notes: Where the question is about one room, laboratory or office.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.notes: Where the question is about what state things are in.

parameters.name: expiring_within_days
parameters.notes: Warranties and insurances falling due. How far in advance the school should be reminded is not specified anywhere (BR-4, OQ-4).

parameters.name: campus_phrase
parameters.notes: Where the question is about one campus of a group (BR-5).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What the school owns and what is about to lapse.

fields.name: assets
fields.description: Identifier, name, category, purchase date, value, location, campus, condition and status.

fields.name: total_value
fields.description: What the register says the school owns. At purchase value — nothing depreciates it (OQ-2).

fields.name: warranty_expiring
fields.description: Warranties running out within the period asked about (BR-4).

fields.name: insurance_expiring
fields.description: Insurance renewals falling due (BR-4).

fields.name: no_warranty_date
fields.description: Assets with no warranty date recorded at all. These will never remind anybody, and the absence looks identical to a warranty that has already run out (BR-4).

fields.name: no_insurance_date
fields.description: The same for insurance. An uninsured asset and an asset whose insurance date nobody entered read the same here (BR-4).

fields.name: unassigned
fields.description: Assets on the register that nobody answers for. Registering assigns to nobody, and nothing forces the next step (BR-9).

fields.name: disposed
fields.description: Assets disposed of. Still on the register and never deleted, so a total that includes them is not what the school owns (BR-8).

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the asset register.
errors.note: The use case writes no exception for it — its eight exceptions are all about registering.

planningRules.rule: Name the assets with no warranty or insurance date at all. A blank date and an expired one look the same on this screen and mean different things: one has lapsed, the other will never warn anybody (BR-4).
Say that the total is at purchase value. Nothing depreciates anything — expected life is recorded and unused — so a register total is what the school paid, not what it holds (OQ-2).
Exclude the disposed assets from any total, and say that they are still on the register. Nothing is ever deleted, so a naive total counts equipment that has already left the school (BR-8).
Name the assets nobody answers for. Registering assigns to nobody and nothing forces an assignment afterwards, so an asset can sit on the register for years with no custodian (BR-9, E8).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: kis kis cheez ki warranty ya insurance khatam hone wali hai?
request.gloss: which things have their warranty or insurance running out?

steps.note: A ninety-day window, stated back — how far ahead the school wants to be told is not written down anywhere (PR-1 concerns the blanks).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the warranties and insurances falling due in the window. Then the list nobody asks for and needs most: the assets with no warranty or insurance date recorded at all — they will never appear on a list like this, and on the screen they are indistinguishable from equipment that is properly covered.

request.text: school ke paas kitne ki cheezein hain?
request.gloss: how much is the school's equipment worth?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the total at purchase value, and say so plainly — nothing in the system depreciates anything, even though every asset carries an expected life. Exclude the disposed assets from the figure and say how many there are: they stay on the register permanently, so a naive total counts equipment that left years ago.

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No asset matches, registered or disposed of.

fields.name: registered

fields.name: changes

fields.name: current_status

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the asset history.
errors.note: The use case writes no exception for it.

planningRules.rule: Give the registration first — the voucher, the value and the date. That is what ties this asset to the books, and it is what somebody checking the register against them is actually after (BR-2, BR-3).

Name the dates that were added later. Between registration and that entry the asset carried no warranty or insurance date and reminded nobody — which is usually the gap somebody is asking about (BR-4).
Say that the value never appears as a change. It is the voucher's and is not editable, so a register value that looks wrong is a voucher question rather than a register one (BR-3).

request.text: is projector ki warranty ki tareekh kis ne aur kab daali thi?
request.gloss: who entered this projector's warranty date and when?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the name and the date it was entered — and the gap it closed: the projector was registered in November and the warranty date was added in February, so for those three months it would have appeared on no warranty list at all. Add the registration itself: the voucher, the value taken from it, and who registered it.
